summary: 100-foot CCC steel fire tower built 1934 on the Chippewa National Forest near Bena, Minnesota; moved in 1976 to the Forest History Center in Grand Rapids, restored 1997, open to climb in season.

facts.design: 100-foot steel tower with a 7 by 7 foot metal cab, built by the Civilian Conservation Corps

access.note: Open during the Forest History Center's regular business hours and closed November through May for safety; no more than four climbers at a time. The Register gives a different season (Memorial Day to October 15).

visit.trail_note: 100 feet, 126 steps to the cab; minimum age 6; proper footwear required; closed during thunderstorms, strong rains and high winds.

events.note: Built by the CCC on the Chippewa National Forest, with a towerman's cabin and garage

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record lists Itasca County, which is the current site in Grand Rapids. The original Boulder Hill site was in Cass County, Chippewa National Forest, Bena District. The story gives both.

The Register says open seven days a week from Memorial Day through October 15. The Forest History Center page says open during regular business hours and closed November through May. The story tells visitors to check hours.

notes_for_editor: The Register text is undated, so the open season may have changed. The record's county (Itasca) is correct for the current site. No pre-1976 fire or staffing records were found in these sources. No photos added.
